newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-Tuigamala poised for international return.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Tuigamala poised for international return.

text.p: CORK, Ireland, Nov 7 - Former All Black wing Va'aiga Tuigamala is poised to make his return to international rugby union, for Western Samoa, on Saturday.

Tuigamala, who has been playing with English club Wasps on loan from rugby league giants Wigan this season, will join the Manu Samoa touring party in this southern Irish city tomorrow and will start Saturday's match against Munster on the reserves bench.

And with Manu Samoa coach Bryan Williams keen to exploit the new substitution rule, which allows substitutes to be used without players having to be medically cleared, Tuigamala will almost certainly get onto Musgrave Park on Saturday.
"Wasps have agreed to release Inga and he will join us tomorrow," Williams told NZPA.
"It's great for us, because it means we have the chance to blend him into the side before the test.
"We are looking at playing him at wing or in the centres."
Manu Samoa have been the unwitting beneficiaries of a dispute between the English clubs and home union international sides playing in the next few weeks.
With Ireland, Scotland and England all in action in coming weeks, the English Courage League clubs sought to have their matches deferred while their players were on international duty.
With Wasps losing players to Ireland and England, that cleared the way for Tuigamala to join up with Manu Samoa.
His appearance on Saturday in a blue jersey would end a three-year absence from international rugby.

The 26-year-old, who members of the British press call "Oddjob" in reference to his resemblance to the James Bond villain, last played for New Zealand in the test loss to England at Twickenham in November 1993.
He joined Wigan soon after and even represented Western Samoa in the rugby league World Cup in 1995.

His exposure to the professional world of rugby league saw Tuigamala develop into a more focused, more physically refined player who was able to use his ball skills effectively while still retaining the power style of play that made him a hit during his Auckland and New Zealand career.
He has been one of the sensations of the English rugby union season, featuring at centre for Wasps and proving a handful for all opposing centres.
The lengthy mid-season break for Wasps could even see Tuigamala staying with Manu Samoa for the match against Cambridge University, and the first two matches of the Welsh leg of the tour as well.
Tuigamala will not be the only former international returning to Western Samoa's ranks, though.

Flanker Junior Paramore, who had a brief liaison with rugby league before joining English second division club Bedford this year, is set to join the touring party on Sunday and will be available for the test against Ireland in Dublin on Tuesday.
"Bedford want Junior to play on Saturday but he will be able to join us on Sunday," Williams added.
"That will bring two more high quality players into the squad, and that can only benefit us."
